doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Chico Hamilton and Arnie Lawrence convince him to teach
summary: He didn't expect to enjoy teaching; Hamilton and Lawrence, founders of the New School jazz program, persuaded him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. But I really love teaching. You know I didn’t think I would like it as much as I did. In fact it was Chico Hamilton and Arnie Lawrence that convinced me. Chico is still there
teaching too, and he was there from the beginning. Arnie isn’t anymore. Arnie moved to Israel where he started a jazz school there.

Yeah. But he was one of the founders of the New School jazz program. So when they asked me to come in and teach the blues I said, “I don’t know,” I said, “I don’t have teaching credentials.” You know I figured if you’re going to teach at a university, you’ve got to have —
